follicular dendritic cell (FDC) maintenance of HIV infecttivity requires the presence of Ab and Fc receptors.
FDCs can maintain the infectivity of HIV immune complexes in vitro in a manner that depends on the presence of specific Abs and FcγR-mediated interactions.
FDC-FcRs are required for FDCs to maintain HIV infectivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which FDCs maintain the infectivity of HIV immune complexes.
the mechanism(s) by which the immune system can maintain HIV infectivity on the surface of FDCs for long periods.
the mechanisms by which HIV infectivity is maintained in the presence of Ab and FcR-bearing cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ab and FDCs, through their FcγRs and the maintenance of infective HIV, are critical to the persistence of HIV infectivity in vivo.
Ab and FCDs are necessary for maintenance of HIV infectivities.
the presence of Abs and FcγR-bearing FDCs is required for the maintenance of HIV infective activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FDCs, through their FcγRs and their ability to trap immune complexes, maintain HIV infectivity in the form of Ab-virus complexes.
FDCs are required to maintain HIV infectivity in the absence of Ab.
HIV infectivity persists on FDCs because of a complex interaction between Ab and FcRs that stabilizes the virion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FDCs are a key player in the maintenance of HIV infective virus in the host.
FDCs can maintain HIV infectivity in the presence of Ab, and this activity is mediated by FcγRs on the FDC.
FcγRs on FDCs are required for maintenance of HIV infectivities in vitro.
